neighbours.label: A vehicle, mount, carried-gear or locomotion token (truck, bus, horse, backpack, walk, drive) whose preceding context places it at rest or in place - parked, tied up, listed as a facility or amenity, used as an object, moving about within a confined spot - rather than travelling along a route toward a destination; the - pole takes the en-route / along / escort reading of the same words.
fire: Besides the loading docks, the site has a staff canteen, a weighbridge, overnight parking and a truck bay.
Tickets for the concert include a hot supper at the pavilion and bus service back to the hotels.
The rider loosened the girth and left her horse tethered in the shade of the stable wall.
When the bench turned out to be wet, he sat on his backpack and waited for the shop to open.
The kitchen was so cramped that the two cooks kept having to walk around each other all evening.
Before refuelling, the ground crew chocked the wheels of the aircraft and parked a fuel truck beside the wing.
Parking behind the hall is never a problem, so just drive in and leave the car wherever there is space.
In the yard behind the farmhouse, parked beside the woodpile, stood an old truck with its bonnet propped open.
quiet: For three days the convoy rolled along the coast road, every truck caked in red dust.
Halfway across the valley the scout urged his horse into a canter toward the distant pass.
Two miles into the climb the heavy backpack was already dragging at her shoulders.
The guide led us along the ridge for an hour, and from there we had to walk the last six miles toward the hut.
Twenty minutes into the journey, still crawling along the ring road, the bus had barely moved in the heavy traffic.
With the escort riding alongside, the royal carriage rattled on through village after village toward the capital.
After hours on the river road they were still driving along in silence when the lights of the city came into view.
Mile after mile the two men kept walking along the empty road toward the harbour.

short: vehicle at rest, not en route
notes: Probes (fraction of max 17.75) split on the frame BEFORE the token, not the token. Matched pairs: ' truck' 0.475 in a facility list ('car park, petrol station and a truck wash') and 0.209 in 'keys in the truck parked' vs 0.067 after 'rumbling along the dusty highway'; ' backpack' 0.498 used as a pillow vs 0.165 'hikers shouldered their backpacks and set off'; ' walk' 0.608 'chairs surrounded me ... had to walk around' vs ' walking' 0.021 'down the dark street'. Also 'tied his horse to the post' 0.403; 'aircraft to park ... service vehicles' 0.400 (peak ' vehicles'); 'parked the van' 0.326; 'with bus transportation' 0.474 vs 'patrol cars roared alongside, escorting' 0.118. Meaning without a locomotion token does not fire: 'paced around the kitchen' 0.011. - pole mirror: ' along' x4, ' escort', ' driving', 'had to walk the 2 km' (-0.73 of -max); logits suppress ' journey', ' along', ' route', promote ' static', ' vacant'. Fire items copy the 0.40-0.61 configs with the at-rest cue in LEFT context (list with 'overnight parking', 'and bus service', dismounted horse, backpack sat on, cramped-kitchen walk, 'parked a fuel truck', parking talk then 'just drive' = corpus 0.74, 'parked ... stood an old truck'). Near misses keep the same single tokens (tokenizer-verified) and put a route cue (along, across the valley, into the climb, into the journey, mile after mile) BEFORE the token. Caveats: 'means of transportation' with no left context scored 0.12, so the cue must precede the noun; peaks smear onto the next token; half the corpus top-16 is non-English, tested in English only.
